title: सङ्‍घीय नेपालको सार्वजनिक वित्त व्यवस्थापन: Fiscal Management of Federal Nepal
nepali: सङ्‍घीय राज्य संरचनाको सबैभन्दा आकर्षक पक्ष ‘वित्तीय सङ्‍घीयता’ जसले सङ्‍घीय राज्य प्रणालीमा सङ्‍घीय एकाइहरूले गर्ने सार्वजनिक वित्त व्यवस्थापन र विभिन्न तहका सरकारहरूबिचको आर्थिक कारोबारलाई परिभाषित र परिचालित गर्छ । खासगरी उपराष्ट्रिय तहहरू (Subnational Levels) लाई दिइने खर्चको जिम्मेवारी, राजस्वको क्षेत्राधिकार, अन्तरसरकारी वित्तीय हस्तान्तरण, वित्तीय पारदर्शिता र आर्थिक सुशासन, उपराष्ट्रिय तहहरूको ऋण उठाउने अधिकार, ऋण दिगोपन वित्तीय सङ्‍घीयताका प्रमुख अवयवहरू हुन् । नेपालको संविधानले सङ्‍घीय, प्रादेशिक र स्थानीयसहित तीनै तहका सरकारहरूलाई ‘आफ्नै’ बजेट तर्जुमा गर्ने अधिकार दिएको छ । अहिले प्रादेशिक र स्थानीय तहको सार्वजनिक वित्त व्यवस्थापनमा सबैभन्दा ठुलो चुनौती मानवस्रोत व्यवस्थापन देखिएको छ । योजना निर्माण, तिनको प्राथमिकीकरण, त्यसअनुरूपको बजेट लेखन, सार्वजनिक खरिद, योजना कार्यान्वयन, खर्च प्रभावकारिता र खर्च अनुगमनसम्मका लागि प्रदेशस्तरमै पनि विषयगत र क्षेत्रगत दक्षता भएका जनशक्ति पाउन र उनीहरूलाई टिकाइराख्न मुस्किल परिरहेको छ । साथमा अनुदान, राजश्व र अन्य आर्थिक स्रोतहरूको बाँडफाँटका सूत्रहरूको पुनरावलोकन र सबै तहमा सार्वजनिक वित्त व्यवस्थापनको क्षमता वृद्धि अपरिहार्य देखिएको छ। यो लेख नेपालको वित्तीय सङ्‍घीयतासम्बद्ध नीतिगत, संरचनागत र सञ्चालनगत पक्षहरूको समीक्षामा केन्द्रित छ ।
american_english: The most attractive aspect of the federal state structure is 'fiscal federalism', which defines and mobilizes public financial management undertaken by federal units in the federal state system and economic transactions among governments at various levels. In particular, the key components of fiscal federalism are the responsibility for expenditure assigned to subnational levels (Subnational Levels), jurisdiction over revenue, intergovernmental financial transfers, financial transparency and economic good governance, the right of subnational levels to raise debt, and debt sustainability. Nepal's constitution has granted all three levels of government — federal, provincial and local — the right to formulate their 'own' budgets. At present, human resource management appears to be the biggest challenge in public financial management at the provincial and local levels. For planning, prioritization of those plans, budget writing accordingly, public procurement, plan implementation, expenditure effectiveness and expenditure monitoring, it has been difficult to secure and retain subject-area and sectoral expertise even at the provincial level. Alongside this, the review of formulas for the distribution of grants, revenue and other economic resources, and the enhancement of public financial management capacity at all levels, appear indispensable. This article is focused on reviewing the policy, structural and operational aspects related to Nepal's fiscal federalism.

informal_english: Federalism's money side — 'fiscal federalism' — is the most eye-catching part of the federal set-up, and it's what defines and runs the public money management that federal units do, plus the economic dealings between governments at different levels. The big pieces of it are things like who's responsible for spending at subnational level, who gets to tax, money moving between governments, keeping the books transparent and the economy well run, subnational bodies being able to borrow, and keeping that borrowing sustainable. Nepal's constitution gives all three levels — federal, provincial and local — the right to draw up their 'own' budgets. Right now, managing people is the biggest headache in public financial management at provincial and local level. It's been a real struggle to get and keep skilled staff, both subject experts and sector experts, even at provincial level, for planning, prioritising plans, writing budgets, procurement, putting plans into action, making sure money is well spent and keeping an eye on it. On top of that, the formulae for sharing out grants, revenue and other economic resources need a look, and building up public financial management capacity at every level seems unavoidable. This piece is focused on reviewing the policy, structural and operational sides of Nepal's fiscal federalism.
